deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is folio 19r of Riemann's draft on the mechanics of the ear (bundle R.Ohr; a version of this material was published posthumously by Henle in 1867 as 'Mechanik des Ohres'). The page finishes a qualitative thermal argument begun on the previous page and opens section IV.

Setting (from the previous page). Let T_b be brain temperature and T_e the external temperature.
- The petrous pyramid contains the carotid canal, so its temperature is close to T_b.
- The other bones around the tympanic cavity contain blood sinuses, large arteries and veins. Mucosa and periosteum shield them against radiating heat into the cavity. So they are warmer than the cavity itself.
- A marginal note gives a rough guess: their deficit below brain temperature might go from about 10 degrees to 20 degrees.

The law invoked ('nach dem oben angeführten Gesetze'). Write the temperature at a point x as T(x) = T_b - (T_b - T_e) f(x), where 0 <= f(x) <= 1 depends only on geometry and on the thermal conductivities and exchange coefficients. This is what you get for steady-state linear heat conduction with fixed internal source temperature T_b and Newton-type exchange with the outside. The deficit T_b - T(x) is therefore proportional to the external deficit T_b - T_e everywhere in the body.

This page. Suppose T_e falls so that T_b - T_e doubles. Then every local deficit doubles: T_b - T'(x) = 2 (T_b - T(x)). Consequences drawn:
- The air-filled tympanic cavity has a large deficit, because its lining is a poor conductor and radiator. Its cooling, equal to the old deficit, is therefore appreciable.
- The surrounding bones have a small deficit, so they cool only very slightly.
- The ossicles lie in the cavity and take on its temperature, so they contract appreciably (linear thermal contraction ΔL = α L ΔT, implicit). The cavity walls stay almost unchanged.

Riemann then states the limit of the argument. Because the thermal properties of the components are unknown, nothing more can be established than this: when the external temperature sinks, the ossicles cool and contract much more strongly than the cavity walls.

Section IV begins. He will determine the changes in the position of the ossicles needed when the external temperature falls, so that all parts meant to be in contact continue to fit exactly onto one another. The next page carries this out with distances between joints: incus–tympanic joint, incus–stapes joint, malleus–incus joint, and the fixed upper end of the manubrium.
errors: No mathematical errors on this page.

The proportional-scaling law assumes a linear, steady-state heat problem with temperature-independent conductivities and unchanged blood flow. Physiologically, peripheral vasoconstriction in the cold would break exact proportionality. Riemann himself treats the conclusion only as qualitative.
'auf das Doppelte' is an illustrative assumption, not a derived value.

results.what: In steady linear heat conduction with fixed source temperature, the deficits below the source temperature scale proportionally with the external deficit; applied to the cooling of the middle ear and the ossicles
results.modern_name: Linearity/superposition of steady-state heat conduction (Newton's law of cooling, Fourier theory)

results.what: Qualitative conclusion: the ossicles contract thermally more than the walls of the tympanic cavity, so the ossicle chain must readjust its position to keep the joint surfaces in contact
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann, Mechanik des Ohres (posthumous 1867); detail of this draft unsure

deep.surprise_reason: Riemann's work on the mechanics of the ear is known and published. This page contains only qualitative physical reasoning based on standard linear heat conduction, with no new mathematics.

checkable.asserts: If T = Tb - (Tb-Te)*f and the external deficit doubles, then the new local deficit is twice the old local deficit.
The local temperature drop equals the old local deficit: large in the cavity (f near 1), small in bones near brain temperature (f near 0).
Linear thermal contraction ΔL = alpha*L*ΔT, with ΔT = -(Tb-Te)*f; contraction is proportional to the local cooling.

transcription_corrections: In 'Gehörknöchelchen werden', the ending of 'Gehörknöchelchen' is overwritten/inserted in the manuscript.
In 'mit den thermischen', 'den' appears corrected from 'dem', and 'thermischen' shows an overwritten letter.
The folio number '11.' appears at top right, and '19' is written in pencil in the margin.
